groups.sentence: Instructors decide and state what documentation, such as prompts, outputs or drafts, students must keep or submit.
Students explain how and why they used AI and what they did with the output.
Instructors ask students to document their AI use, submit drafts or version history, and reflect on their process.
Students submit the full AI chat transcript, prompts and outputs, as an appendix or with their assignment.
Instructors may require students to submit AI transcripts, prompts, process documents or reflections.
Students save their prompts, chats and AI use log and are ready to provide them.
Students discuss their own contributions and reflect on their AI use and its effect on learning.
Students may be asked to submit transcripts, prompts, documentation or reflections on their AI use.
Students keep their drafts, AI logs and records of AI use.
Students keep drafts, notes and version histories as evidence of their own work process.
Everyone using AI keeps records of AI use, such as tools, prompts and decisions.
Students submit a written reflection on their AI use, its limits and its effect on their learning.
Students provide their original pre-AI draft or original assignment alongside the AI-assisted version.
When AI misuse is suspected, instructors may ask students for drafts, prompt logs or process records.
Documentation, logs and reflections on AI use are used in various ways, and some instructors require them.
